operations.title: Research state for BSSC private-message sum-capacity
operations.summary: For the stated binary-input broadcast channel, the exact private-message sum-capacity remains open. The governed benchmark is 0.361642884421954615663441578150587… ≤ C_sum ≤ 0.369316568803963. The accepted structural and finite-grid auxiliary-receiver results improve neither endpoint; the three-point-grid value is not a capacity upper bound, and midpoint localization is only a necessary condition relative to a supplied threshold.

operations.title: Auxiliary-receiver outer-bound program
operations.summary: This program studies the Gohari–Liu–Nair two-auxiliary-receiver outer-bound formulation through input-only structural reductions, finite-posterior-grid receiver cardinality, exact symbolic finite-grid certificates, midpoint coercivity, and a possible bridge to the full continuum functional. It currently establishes no continuum cardinality theorem, grid-convergence or infimum-interchange theorem, reflected-pair sufficiency, certified global minimization of B(G,K), improved achievable rate, or improved universal converse. Identification with the external manuscript remains conditional on source transcription fidelity.

operations.title: Input-only reduction for the auxiliary receivers
operations.summary: For finite auxiliary-receiver laws whose constraints use only audited single-output quantities, replacing T_{G,K|X,Y,Z} by the product of its induced input-only marginals preserves the relevant G- and K-based mutual informations, leaves the Y- and Z-marginal terms unchanged, and preserves constraint systems formed from those quantities. The reduction does not cover joint or output-conditioned terms such as I(S;G,K|R) or I(S;Y|G), and its application to every cited manuscript branch remains conditional on transcription fidelity.

operations.title: Receiver cardinality on a finite posterior grid
operations.summary: For a fixed N-point posterior grid Q containing 0, 1/2, and 1, each finite-output binary-input receiver in the fair-input grid-restricted auxiliary optimization can be replaced by one with at most N outputs without changing the restricted LP value. The result follows by preserving the posterior mean and the N−2 nonendpoint information samples and applying Carathéodory in dimension N−1. It does not require the replacement atoms to lie on Q and does not establish continuum cardinality, grid convergence, infimum interchange, or continuum reflected-pair sufficiency.

operations.title: Exact auxiliary-receiver optimum on the three-point posterior grid
operations.summary: For Q₀={0,1/2,1} and c=h₂(1/4)−1/2, the supplied encoded 30-row formulation has exact receiver infimum inf_{G,K} V_{Q₀}(G,K)=inf_m V_{Q₀}(m,m°)=c. A W=X witness supplies the universal lower bound, while a reflection-invariant revealing-erasure posterior measure supplies the matching reflected-pair construction. The direct W=X checker is missing as documented, manuscript-row fidelity is unverified, and the result is only a lower approximation to the fixed-receiver functional rather than a capacity converse.

operations.title: Midpoint-information coercive lower bound
operations.summary: For g=I_G(1/2), k=I_K(1/2), c=h₂(1/4)−1/2, and F(x)=2c·max{c,x}/(c+x), the encoded 30-row Q₀ problem satisfies B(G,K)≥V₀(g,k)≥max{F(g),F(k)}. For c≤U<2c, B(G,K)≤U necessarily implies 2c²/U−c≤g,k≤Uc/(2c−U). The result is an exact-symbolically audited necessary localization bound for the encoded rows, not a sufficient condition, global minimization, reflected-optimality theorem, or capacity converse; external row fidelity remains unverified.

operations.title: Fidelity of the external Theorem 9 transcription
operations.summary: The supplied evidence does not include the complete external equations (19a)–(19p) or an independently checkable manuscript formulation. It therefore remains unresolved whether the single-output audit is exhaustive, all 30 encoded rows reproduce the manuscript, side-condition orientations are correct, and every coefficient was transcribed correctly. The structural arguments remain supported for systems with the stated form, and the symbolic code certifies the encoded rows only after accepting their transcription.

operations.title: Reproducibility status of the three-point-grid certificates
operations.summary: The supplied frontier-global-bridge checker does not directly audit the documented W=X witness table; it is byte-for-byte the coercivity checker supplied as frontier-q0-coercive. The two commands therefore execute duplicate mathematical content and are not independent corroborations. This documentation defect does not invalidate the encoded finite-grid conclusions: the checker verifies the stronger coercive bound and matching upper row, while the prose and row table carry the direct W=X argument. Certification remains limited to the hard-coded rows.

operations.title: Bridge from finite posterior grids to the full receiver functional
operations.summary: No supplied result bridges the accepted structural and finite-grid analysis to a certified global optimization of the full receiver functional B(G,K). Missing ingredients include a continuum receiver-output cardinality bound, convergence of finite-grid optimizations, interchange of the receiver infimum with the grid limit, reflected-pair sufficiency or optimality, and certified global minimization. The finite-grid optimum and midpoint coercivity remain lower approximations or necessary localization tools and do not yield a universal capacity converse.
